title: The Issues Practice

header.html: Explain the purpose of the issues practice and its relationships with the principles; explain the purpose of the issue management approach, issue register and issue report; define issue and its types, project baseline and change control; describe baselines, issue resolution, change control, delegating authority for changes and the change budget
the official PRINCE2 7 Foundation syllabus (PeopleCert), learning outcome 4.6

html:
1Purpose

The issues practice captures, assesses and manages issues so that they are resolved or escalated and the project stays under control. It also handles changes to the project baseline in a controlled way.

2Key concepts

Term Meaning
Issue A relevant event that has happened, was not planned, and needs management action
Project baseline The approved version of the project's products and plans used as the reference for control
Change control The process that makes sure changes to baselines are assessed, approved and recorded

Types of issue

Type Meaning
Request for change A proposal to change a baseline
Off-specification Something required that is not (or will not be) provided as specified
Problem or concern Any other matter the project manager must resolve or escalate
Business opportunity An issue that offers a chance to improve the business case (sometimes raised as a change)

[Verify live] The exact list of types in the official book.

Exam tip

. Risk = might happen. Issue = has happened. Request for change and off-specification are types of issue, not risks.

3Guidance

Guidance Meaning
Baselines Approved products and plans; changes need control
Issue resolution Capture, assess, propose, decide, implement (the issue technique)
Change control Assess impact on cost, time, quality, scope, benefits, risk and sustainability, then approve or reject
Delegating authority for changes The project board may give the change authority or the project manager power to approve changes within limits
Change budget A sum of money the board sets aside to pay for approved changes

The issue technique: capture, assess, propose, decide, implement. [Verify live]

4Management products

Product Purpose
Issue management approach (PID) How issues and changes are managed on this project
Issue register (project log) A record of all issues, their status and decisions
Issue report A detailed description of one issue (or a request for change or off-specification), with analysis and recommendation
Exam tip

. Request for change and off-specification are issue types. Change control applies to changes to baselines.

Exam tip

. The change budget is set aside by the board to pay for approved changes.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A user asks for an extra feature after the requirements were baselined. Which type of issue is this?

  • AOff-specification
  • BA risk
  • CRequest for change
  • DA benefit
Show the answer

Answer: C. A proposal to change a baseline is a request for change.

S2Which statements are CORRECT? (1) An issue has already happened. (2) An off-specification is something that is not provided as specified. (3) An issue is something that might happen. (4) A change budget is a risk allowance.

  • A3 and 4
  • B1 and 2
  • C2 and 3
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: B. Issues have happened, and off-specifications are not as specified.

S3Identify the missing word. A [ ? ] is the approved version of products and plans used as the reference for control.

  • ABaseline
  • BTolerance
  • CStage
  • DDependency
Show the answer

Answer: A. That is a baseline.

S4The board sets aside money to pay for approved changes. What is it called?

  • AContingency plan
  • BChange budget
  • CRisk budget
  • DStage reserve
Show the answer

Answer: B. The board provides a change budget.

S5Which management product describes one issue in detail with analysis and a recommendation?

  • AIssue register
  • BIssue report
  • CDaily log
  • DQuality register
Show the answer

Answer: B. The issue report covers one issue in detail.

S6Who may be given authority to approve changes within limits?

  • AAny team member
  • BProject support only
  • CNobody
  • DThe change authority or the project manager, as delegated by the board
Show the answer

Answer: D. The board can delegate change authority within limits.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Define an issue.

Show the answer

A relevant event that has happened, was not planned and needs management action.

R2Name the types of issue.

Show the answer

Request for change, off-specification, problem or concern, and business opportunity.

R3What is change control?

Show the answer

The process that assesses, approves and records changes to baselines.

R4What is the change budget?

Show the answer

Money set aside by the board to pay for approved changes.

R5What does the issue register record?

Show the answer

All issues, their status and decisions.

R6Name the five steps of the issue technique.

Show the answer

Capture, assess, propose, decide and implement.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Issue has happened, unplanned, needs action
Types request for change, off-specification, problem or concern, business opportunity
Baseline / change control approved reference / assess, approve, record changes
Authority change authority; change budget
Products issue management approach, issue register, issue report
